<description>
**Problem:** On Arch Linux the installed `bitcoin` command doesn't work: `bitcoin -m node`, `bitcoin chainstate`, and similar commands all fail with `execvp failed to execute ... No such file or directory` (#35785). Arch installs the programs the wrapper runs into a different directory than the wrapper looks in.

**Solution:** Make the wrapper look for those programs in the directory they were actually installed to, rather than a hardcoded one. Small change to the wrapper (`src/bitcoin.cpp`), plus build-system changes to pass it the configured install directories, and a functional test for the installed layout. Details are in the commit messages.

Fixes #35785. Built from earlier PRs #36037, #35789, and #36085.
</description>

<commits>
56d9cb6032 test: characterize installed bitcoin wrapper libexec lookup

Add a functional test for the installed-layout executable lookup in the
`bitcoin` wrapper. When installed in a `bin/` directory the wrapper looks
for internal binaries like `bitcoind` in a sibling directory under the
same prefix; this path is never exercised by the normal build-tree tests
because every binary sits next to the wrapper there.

The test builds a fake install prefix under tmpdir, copies the wrapper
into `bin/` and `bitcoind` into an internal directory (not next to the
wrapper), and runs the wrapper by absolute path with PATH cleared so a
lookup miss cannot be satisfied by an unrelated system binary. Under
--valgrind, resolve the valgrind executable via shutil.which() before PATH
is blanked, since subprocess.run() resolves a bare command name against
the env it is given rather than the calling process's real PATH.

This characterizes current behavior — the wrapper resolves binaries from
hardcoded `bin/` and `libexec/` directories — so a following commit can
change it to honor CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR and CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBEXECDIR and
verify the result. Also add the absolute CMAKE_INSTALL_FULL_BINDIR and
CMAKE_INSTALL_FULL_LIBEXECDIR values to test/config.ini.in, and lay out the
fake install tree from the bindir name and the relative path from bindir to
libexecdir, so the test covers both relative settings (the default) and
absolute ones (as Nix passes them). Include GNUInstallDirs at the top level
before add_subdirectory(test) so these variables are set when config.ini is
generated.

Adapted from https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36037.

Co-Authored-By: cyb3ralbert <cyberalbert@protonmail.ch>
Co-Authored-By: Hennadii Stepanov <32963518+hebasto@users.noreply.github.com>

76bf68ec05 build: respect CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR/LIBEXECDIR in bitcoin wrapper

Switch from hardcoded "bin"/"libexec" strings to CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR and
CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBEXECDIR in the installed-layout executable lookup, so the
wrapper works on distributions that configure non-default install
directories. Previously `bitcoin -m node`, `bitcoin chainstate`, and
similar subcommands failed with "execvp failed to execute" on Arch Linux,
which sets CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBEXECDIR=lib (#35785).

Have CMake compute the name of the bindir and the path from the bindir to
the libexecdir (e.g. "bin" and "../libexec") from CMAKE_INSTALL_FULL_BINDIR
and CMAKE_INSTALL_FULL_LIBEXECDIR, and thread both values through
bitcoin-build-config.h. Using the FULL values means the lookup works whether
the settings are relative to the install prefix or absolute, as Nix sets
them. Add configure-time FATAL_ERROR guards for empty values (complement to
the compile-time static_asserts). Remove the now-redundant
include(GNUInstallDirs) from InstallBinaryComponent.cmake.

Fixes #35785.

The fix and test build on #36037, #35789, and #36085.

index 1743d79f44..79ed3593d4 100644
--- a/cmake/bitcoin-build-config.h.in
+++ b/cmake/bitcoin-build-config.h.in
@@ -100,6 +100,17 @@
 /* Define to the home page for this package. */
 #define CLIENT_URL "@PROJECT_HOMEPAGE_URL@"
 
+/* Name of the install directory for public executables (last component of
+   CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR, e.g. "bin"). Used by the bitcoin wrapper to recognize
+   when it is running from an installed layout. */
+#define BITCOIN_BINDIR_NAME "@BITCOIN_BINDIR_NAME@"
+
+/* Install directory for internal executables, relative to the install
+   directory for public executables (e.g. "../libexec"). Used by the bitcoin
+   wrapper to locate bitcoind, bitcoin-node, bitcoin-gui, etc. in an installed
+   layout. */
+#define BITCOIN_INTERNAL_LIBEXECDIR "@BITCOIN_BINDIR_TO_LIBEXECDIR@"
+
 /* Define to the version of this package. */
 #define CLIENT_VERSION_STRING "@CLIENT_VERSION_STRING@"
 
diff --git a/src/bitcoin.cpp b/src/bitcoin.cpp
index b5db618a32..ac45af0629 100644
--- a/src/bitcoin.cpp
+++ b/src/bitcoin.cpp
@@ -18,6 +18,13 @@
 #include <tinyformat.h>
 #include <vector>
 
+// Guard against empty install dir values; they would silently break
+// ExecCommand()'s installed-layout lookup. CMakeLists.txt computes both values
+// from the configured install directories and never leaves them empty; these
+// static_asserts are a backstop.
+static_assert(BITCOIN_BINDIR_NAME[0] != '\0', "BITCOIN_BINDIR_NAME must not be empty");
+static_assert(BITCOIN_INTERNAL_LIBEXECDIR[0] != '\0', "BITCOIN_INTERNAL_LIBEXECDIR must not be empty");
+
 const TranslateFn G_TRANSLATION_FUN{nullptr};
 
 static constexpr auto HELP_USAGE = R"(Usage: %s [OPTIONS] COMMAND...
@@ -173,8 +180,8 @@ bool UseMultiprocess(const CommandLine& cmd)
 }
 
 //! Execute the specified bitcoind, bitcoin-qt or other command line in `args`
-//! using src, bin and libexec directory paths relative to this executable, where
-//! the path to this executable is specified in `wrapper_argv0`.
+//! using src, bin and the configured libexec directory paths relative to this
+//! executable, where the path to this executable is specified in `wrapper_argv0`.
 //!
 //! @param args Command line arguments to execute, where first argument should
 //!             be a relative path to a bitcoind, bitcoin-qt or other executable
@@ -229,9 +236,10 @@ static void ExecCommand(const std::vector<const char*>& args, std::string_view w
     // (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31375#discussion_r1861814807)
     const bool fallback_os_search{!fs::PathFromString(std::string{wrapper_argv0}).has_parent_path()};
 
-    // If wrapper is installed in a bin/ directory, look for target executable
-    // in libexec/
-    (wrapper_dir.filename() == "bin" && try_exec(wrapper_dir.parent_path() / "libexec" / arg0.filename())) ||
+    // If wrapper is installed in the bindir (e.g. bin/), look for the target
+    // executable in the configured internal-executable directory (libexecdir),
+    // using the path from the bindir to the libexecdir (e.g. ../libexec).
+    (wrapper_dir.filename() == BITCOIN_BINDIR_NAME && try_exec((wrapper_dir / BITCOIN_INTERNAL_LIBEXECDIR / arg0.filename()).lexically_normal())) ||
 #ifdef WIN32
     // Otherwise check the "daemon" subdirectory in a windows install.
     (!wrapper_dir.empty() && try_exec(wrapper_dir / "daemon" / arg0.filename())) ||
diff --git a/CMakeLists.txt b/CMakeLists.txt
index 7317dd3e13..40e12f2a33 100644
--- a/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -654,6 +654,32 @@ if(CMAKE_VERSION VERSION_GREATER_EQUAL 3.29)
   set(CMAKE_SKIP_TEST_ALL_DEPENDENCY FALSE)
 endif()
 
+# Populate CMAKE_INSTALL_FULL_BINDIR, CMAKE_INSTALL_FULL_LIBEXECDIR, etc.
+# before the subdirectories below, which substitute these values into generated
+# files (test/config.ini and src/bitcoin-build-config.h).
+include(GNUInstallDirs)
+# GNUInstallDirs provides non-empty defaults; only explicit user overrides can
+# produce empty values, which would silently break the installed-layout lookup
+# in src/bitcoin.cpp. Catch that at configure time.
+if(NOT CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR)
+  message(FATAL_ERROR "CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR must not be empty")
+endif()
+if(NOT CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBEXECDIR)
+  message(FATAL_ERROR "CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBEXECDIR must not be empty")
+endif()
+# Values the bitcoin wrapper uses to find internal executables in an installed
+# layout: the name of the bindir, and the path from the bindir to the
+# libexecdir. They are computed from the absolute CMAKE_INSTALL_FULL_* values,
+# so they are right whether CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR and CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBEXECDIR
+# are relative to the install prefix (e.g. "bin" and "libexec") or absolute (as
+# Nix sets them), and they don't depend on the prefix when both are relative,
+# so `cmake --install --prefix` still works.
+cmake_path(GET CMAKE_INSTALL_FULL_BINDIR FILENAME BITCOIN_BINDIR_NAME)
+file(RELATIVE_PATH BITCOIN_BINDIR_TO_LIBEXECDIR "${CMAKE_INSTALL_FULL_BINDIR}" "${CMAKE_INSTALL_FULL_LIBEXECDIR}")
+if(NOT BITCOIN_BINDIR_TO_LIBEXECDIR)
+  set(BITCOIN_BINDIR_TO_LIBEXECDIR ".")
+endif()
+
 add_subdirectory(test)
 add_subdirectory(doc)
 
diff --git a/test/functional/tool_bitcoin.py b/test/functional/tool_bitcoin.py
index 4a39e14360..91dd7d6dfe 100755
--- a/test/functional/tool_bitcoin.py
+++ b/test/functional/tool_bitcoin.py
@@ -11,7 +11,11 @@ from test_framework.util import (
     assert_equal,
 )
 
+import os
 import re
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+from pathlib import Path
 
 
 class ToolBitcoinTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
@@ -75,6 +79,79 @@ class ToolBitcoinTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
             append_config(node.datadir_path, ["ipcbind=unix"])
             self.test_args([], [], expect_exe="bitcoin-node")
 
+        self.test_installed_layout()
+
+    def test_installed_layout(self):
+        """Check how an installed bitcoin wrapper resolves internal executables.
+
+        When the wrapper is installed into a `bin/` directory, it looks for
+        internal executables (bitcoind, bitcoin-node, ...) in a sibling
+        directory under the same install prefix. The normal build-tree tests
+        never exercise this because every binary sits next to the wrapper, so
+        build a fake install prefix and invoke the wrapper by absolute path.
+        """
+        paths = self.get_binaries().paths
+        exeext = self.config["environment"]["EXEEXT"]
+        # Install directories configured at build time. CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR and
+        # CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBEXECDIR can be relative to the install prefix (the
+        # default) or absolute (Nix passes absolute paths), so config.ini has
+        # the absolute CMAKE_INSTALL_FULL_* values. The fake install tree only
+        # needs to reproduce the bindir name and the relative path from bindir
+        # to libexecdir, e.g. "bin" and "../libexec".
+        bindir = Path(self.config["environment"]["BINDIR"])
+        libexecdir = Path(os.path.relpath(self.config["environment"]["LIBEXECDIR"], bindir))
+        prefix = Path(self.options.tmpdir) / "fake-prefix"
+        datadir = self.nodes[0].datadir_path / "wrapper-datadir"
+        datadir.mkdir()
+
+        def copy_exe(src, dest):
+            shutil.copy2(src, dest)
+            # Windows builds with shared dependencies (e.g. vcpkg's
+            # x64-windows-release triplet) keep the DLLs next to the executables
+            # in the build directory, and the copied executables can't start
+            # without them, so copy them too.
+            for dll in Path(src).parent.glob("*.dll"):
+                shutil.copy2(dll, Path(dest).parent / dll.name)
+
+        def make_layout(name, internal_dir):
+            # Lay out <prefix>/<name>/.../<bindir name>/bitcoin and
+            # <bindir>/<internal_dir>/bitcoind, nesting the bindir deep enough
+            # that ".." components in internal_dir stay inside <prefix>/<name>.
+            wrapper_dir = prefix / name / Path(*["sub"] * internal_dir.parts.count("..")) / bindir.name
+            internal_path = Path(os.path.normpath(wrapper_dir / internal_dir))
+            wrapper_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
+            internal_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+            wrapper = wrapper_dir / f"bitcoin{exeext}"
+            copy_exe(paths.bitcoin_bin, wrapper)
+            # `bitcoin node` (with no -ipc* option) execs `bitcoind`. Placing
+            # bitcoind only in the internal directory, not next to the wrapper,
+            # forces the wrapper to resolve it through the bindir -> internal-dir
+            # lookup rather than finding it as a sibling.
+            copy_exe(paths.bitcoind, internal_path / f"bitcoind{exeext}")
+            return wrapper
+
+        def run_wrapper(wrapper):
+            valgrind_cmd = self.nodes[0].binaries.valgrind_cmd
+            if valgrind_cmd:
+                # which(): PATH is blanked below, so resolve valgrind now.
+                valgrind_cmd = [shutil.which(valgrind_cmd[0]) or valgrind_cmd[0], *valgrind_cmd[1:]]
+            env = os.environ.copy()
+            # The wrapper is invoked by absolute path; blank out PATH so a lookup
+            # miss cannot be satisfied by an unrelated bitcoind on the system.
+            env["PATH"] = ""
+            return subprocess.run(valgrind_cmd + [wrapper, "node", f"-datadir={datadir}", "-version"],
+                                  capture_output=True, env=env, timeout=60)
+
+        self.log.info(f"Ensure installed wrapper finds internal binaries in configured {libexecdir}/")
+        result = run_wrapper(make_layout("found", libexecdir))
+        assert_equal(result.returncode, 0)
+        assert_equal(get_exe_name(result.stdout), b"bitcoind")
+
+        other_dir = libexecdir.with_name(libexecdir.name + "_notfound")
+        self.log.info(f"Ensure installed wrapper does not find internal binaries in unconfigured {other_dir}/")
+        result = run_wrapper(make_layout("notfound", other_dir))
+        assert result.returncode != 0, f"wrapper unexpectedly ran bitcoind from {other_dir}/: {result.stdout!r}"
+
 
 def get_node_output(node):
     ret = node.process.wait(timeout=60)
